The cognate family is clear, though the nominal meanings are not identical in every language.

DEDR 1911 identifies Kannada kūḻ (ಕೂಳು) ‘boiled rice, food’ as part of Proto-Dravidian *kūḻ ‘porridge’. Tamil kūḻ means thick gruel/porridge; Tulu kūru/kūlu/kūḷu means boiled rice. This is a genuine cognate set, but the meanings range from porridge to boiled rice and food; it should not be treated as an exact synonym for every use of ‘food’.

Comparative evidence: DEDR 1818 lists Tamil kuḻi ‘pit, hole, hollow, cavity, depression, excavation’; Kannada kuḻi ‘hollow, hole, pit, grave’; Tulu guri / guḷi ‘hole, pit’. The dictionary reconstructs Proto-Dravidian *kuḻ-V ‘pit, hollow’. This supports the Dravidian comparison; exact fit for every sense of ಕಂದಕ should still be judged in context.

Tulu iḷijārů is recorded with the meanings ‘a slope, slipperiness’; it is analysed in the DEDR entry with iḷi- ‘slip out or down, slide’ (DEDR 503) and jār- ‘slip, slide down’ (DEDR 2482). This is a direct Tulu lexical comparison, not evidence for a Proto-Dravidian compound or a verified Tamil cognate.
